context:
Goal: mailaudit's runs skip the work a passing branch already proved, as other repos do.
Problem (rule): the shared skip tool looks for one job named `suite`, but mailaudit's `suite` runs as three parts named `suite (1)` to `suite (3)`, so the skip never fires; a lane tried to fix it and failed its third review round.
Based on (read): a reviewer ran the shared tool's real reader at 00:54 CST: it lists every pull-request job except four named ones, and a job named like `suite (N)` is never matched.
Based on (ruling): decisions/uniform-over-variants (owner, 2026-10-27 12:51 CDT): a repo changes to fit the shared format, never the tool to fit a repo. This item is asked because option a changes a lot in mailaudit and a fourth review round needs your grant.
Departs from: main — the shared skip finds only a job named exactly `suite`; option a renames mailaudit's jobs, option b makes the shared tool read split names, option c changes nothing.
Meanwhile: the work is saved on a branch and mailaudit keeps its own skip step; nothing waits.

options.gain: Mailaudit follows the shared tool, as your rule says a repo should.
options.how: Mailaudit's test job is split into three separate jobs, each with its own name, so the shared skip can find them.
options.label: Change mailaudit: replace its three-part test job with three plain jobs
options.lose: A large change in mailaudit for one skip, and a new run to prove it.

options.gain: Mailaudit needs no change, and any repo with split test jobs works.
options.how: The shared skip action learns job names written like `suite (1)`, `suite (2)`, `suite (3)`.
options.label: Change the shared skip tool so it reads three-part test jobs
options.lose: A shared tool changes to fit one repo, which goes against your ruling.

options.gain: No new work and no risk to the shared tool.
options.how: Nothing changes. The skip for mailaudit stays in its own workflow step.
options.label: Leave it parked; mailaudit keeps its own hand-written skip step
options.lose: Mailaudit keeps a skip step that the shared tool does not cover.

ref: mailaudit lane push-skip-main-run (failed review round 3 of 3), archive branch archive/push-skip-main-run
reply: Count for your 13:33 CST question (is split test running common?), from the coordinator at 13:36 CST, each read from the repo's main workflows by runner 11, runner 12 and the coordinator (claude-settings by a checkout read that may lag): 5 of 8 repos split their tests. Yes: claude-settings (lane-touched-tests.yml, computed matrix), degen (jobs server and app, 2 and 6 legs), q_max (job test, shown test (1) to test (12)), banchi (ci-check per target, 5 targets), mailaudit (suite (1) to suite (3)). No: home, ios-adblock, joyous. So a split form is common, but the exact name `suite (N)` is used only in mailaudit; the others name theirs differently. Reading it against your ruling: option b would teach the shared skip a form used in 5 of 8 repos, which looks like a shared feature, not one repo's variant; but the tool would need to read each repo's different job names, not just `suite (N)`, so the work is wider than the option says. Recommendation unchanged (c) until you say b is fine. Item stays open for your pick.

title: Mailaudit's split test job is invisible to the shared skip: change mailaudit, change the shared tool, or leave it?
why: The coordinator recommends c: it costs nothing and mailaudit still has a working skip. Option b goes against your ruling, so it is never recommended.
